title: The Loudest Sound in History Was Heard 3,000 Miles Away

scenes.text: The loudest sound in history was heard 3,000 miles away.
August 1883. A volcano called Krakatoa blew itself apart in Indonesia.
Forty miles away, sailors on a passing ship had their eardrums burst.
At a hundred miles, it was still 172 decibels. The pressure wave circled the planet three and a half times.
The blast was 200 megatons, about four times the biggest nuclear bomb ever tested.
Three thousand miles away, people heard it and thought it was distant cannon fire.

description:
The 1883 eruption of Krakatoa produced the loudest sound in recorded history, heard about 3,000 miles away on the island of Rodrigues.
Sailors on a ship 40 miles away had their eardrums ruptured, the sound was still about 172 decibels 100 miles out, and the pressure wave was recorded circling the Earth about three and a half times. The explosion released roughly 200 megatons of energy and triggered tsunamis over 100 feet high.
What's the loudest thing you've ever heard? Comment below.
first_comment: The ash from Krakatoa turned sunsets blood red around the world for months. Some think it inspired the sky in Munch's painting The Scream. Would you rather have been 40 miles away or 3,000?
